name: Grammarly
tagline: Grammar, clarity, tone, and AI writing assistant across apps

pricing.notes: Official plan URL checked; public 2026 coverage commonly references Grammarly Pro/Premium around $30/month, with annual pricing lower and branding evolving under Superhuman.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 2,000 AI prompts/member/month; up to 149 seats; 1 style guide; 1 brand tone; 2 groups.
tiers.notes: Also offered quarterly at $60 per 3 months ($20/month effective); annual total is $144.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited prompts, members, style guides, brand tones, and groups.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + quarterly + annual for Pro; Enterprise is custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Additional Pro seats are prorated. A 7-day trial is available only for eligible accounts.

verdictSummary: You can build grammar checks and rewrites, but Grammarly's moat is cross-app extensions, inline UX, enterprise controls, writing telemetry, and long-running language quality.
coreLoopDIY: Run text through LanguageTool plus an LLM rewrite/tone checker, expose a browser extension or local editor.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because suggestions appear inside the apps where writing actually happens.

priorArt.name: LanguageTool
priorArt.desc: Open-source grammar and style checker and the primary Grammarly-like prior art.

alternatives.name: Apple Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Proofread, rewrite, shorten, or change tone almost anywhere, assuming your Apple hardware made the guest list.

facts.install: Built into supported iPhone, iPad and Mac operating systems
facts.engines: Apple on-device foundation models, Private Cloud Compute for larger requests, and optional ChatGPT
facts.dataFormat: Text is processed on-device when possible; larger requests can use stateless Private Cloud Compute, while optional ChatGPT sends the selected text to OpenAI
facts.gapVsPaid: It is restricted to supported Apple hardware and offers fewer continuous cross-app style, brand and writing analytics controls than Grammarly.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Apple Intelligence-compatible hardware, a supported OS, language and region

alternatives.name: Harper
alternatives.desc: A fast English grammar checker that stays on your device and mostly keeps its opinions to itself.

alternatives.name: Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Select text anywhere, hit a hotkey, and fix, rewrite, summarize, or obey a custom instruction without opening another tab.

facts.install: Download the native or portable app, configure a provider or local model, then use the global hotkey
facts.engines: Gemini, OpenAI-compatible APIs, Ollama, llama.cpp, KoboldCPP, TabbyAPI and vLLM
facts.dataFormat: API keys and settings stay locally; selected text goes to the chosen provider or local model, and transient history is cleared when the app closes
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a manual select-text-and-hotkey workflow rather than Grammarly's continuous inline underlines and suggestions across supported apps.
facts.setupBlocker: A model API key or a separately running local model is required; some operating systems may warn about an unsigned or unrecognized binary

alternatives.name: WritingTool
alternatives.desc: A LibreOffice extension with long-document checks, style statistics, profiles, and local AI; installing Java is the cover charge.

facts.install: Install Java 17 or newer, LibreOffice 24.2 or newer and the WritingTool extension
facts.engines: LanguageTool plus optional OpenAI-compatible services, especially a local LocalAI server
facts.dataFormat: Documents remain normal LibreOffice files; checking is local unless a remote LanguageTool or AI endpoint is configured
facts.gapVsPaid: It is centered on LibreOffice rather than working continuously across browsers, email and arbitrary desktop apps like Grammarly.
facts.setupBlocker: Java and LibreOffice are mandatory, and optional AI needs a separately configured service

rejectedAlternatives.name: LanguageTool Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The engine is open source, but the browser extension went Premium-only in 2026; the free web checker no longer replaces across-app use.

notes: An important 'kinda': grammar checking is open-source, cross-app UX is the hard product.
prompt:
Build me a personal writing checker to replace Grammarly. Requirements:

- Grammar engine: LanguageTool running locally via its official Docker image;
  grammar checks never leave my machine.
- A local web page (Node + Express, binds to localhost): paste text, see
  LanguageTool issues underlined with hover explanations, click a suggestion
  to apply it.
- An LLM rewrite pane (key in .env) with three buttons: tighten, friendlier,
  formal. Show a diff against my original before I accept anything.
- A personal dictionary file (dictionary.txt) of names and jargon to never
  flag, passed to LanguageTool on every check.
- CLI mode: `check <file.md>` prints issues with line numbers, exits nonzero
  if any, so it can run as a git pre-commit hook on docs.
- Everything local except the optional LLM call; no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: a browser extension and inline suggestions inside Gmail,
  Docs, or Slack. This is a destination I paste into, that is the honest
  trade against Grammarly.
- README: Docker setup for LanguageTool, the roughly 1 GB of RAM it wants,
  and where the LLM key goes.
